about:
Carolina Metal Fabricators operates from Raleigh, North Carolina, providing structural and miscellaneous steel fabrication for industrial clients across the East Coast. The company emphasizes advanced technology, including software-driven machinery and robotic systems, to achieve accurate and timely delivery to job sites.

The shop focuses on plate fabrication and the processing of various alloys, utilizing a streamlined facility staffed by experienced craftsmen. Its equipment lineup features cutting-edge robotics, which the company describes as among the most advanced on the East Coast, supporting both structural and miscellaneous steel projects.

The company serves a broad range of industrial sectors, positioning itself as a fabricator of choice for industrial segments along the East Coast. Customer types include industrial contractors and manufacturers requiring structural steel components and miscellaneous metalwork.

Carolina Metal Fabricators differentiates itself through its investment in proprietary software and robotic machinery, which it says enables quick turnaround with 100 percent dimensional accuracy. The firm was founded on the premise that technology-driven fabrication can reduce lead times while maintaining quality for demanding industrial applications.

name: Carolina Solar Energy III, LLC
old_description: An architect emeritus, building contractor, solar installer and real estate developer, Richard founded CSE in 2004. Through his leadership, CSE built the first utility-scale solar energy project in the Southeast in 2007. Richard is a lead policy advocate in NC for renewable energy and energy efficiency, past Chair of the NC Sustainable Energy Association and founder of the Carolinas Clean Energy Business Association.
about:
Carolina Solar Energy (CSE) was founded in 2004 in Durham, North Carolina, by Richard Harkrader, an architect emeritus, building contractor, and solar installer. The family-owned business began with a goal to demonstrate that renewable energy legislation could build a solar industry in the state. After years of trial and error, Harkrader completed the first utility-scale solar project in the Southeast at NC State University in 2007. Business partner Gerry Dudzik joined that same year, bringing permitting experience from the cellular tower industry. In 2012, Richard's daughter Carson Harkrader joined after a career at GE Energy, and she assumed leadership in 2018 when both founders retired.

The company develops utility-scale photovoltaic (PV) solar projects across the Southeast and Gulf South, with over 950 MWdc of projects operating or under construction. Its core services include site selection, interconnection applications, state permitting, landowner outreach, community relations, and policy advocacy. The team manages projects from early development through construction, collaborating with municipalities, utilities, and landowners. CSE also operates an intern program and has partnered with organizations like TROSA to provide workforce opportunities.

CSE serves utilities, municipal governments, and private landowners throughout North Carolina, Virginia, Kentucky, and Louisiana. Notable partners include the City of Raleigh, which completed its first major solar development with CSE, and Person County, which hosts three photovoltaic facilities totaling approximately five megawatts. The company focuses on bringing economic development to underserved areas and works with families who have managed land for generations.

CSE distinguishes itself through early-market entry and policy leadership. It was the first solar company to apply for Kentucky state-level permits in March 2020, and its advocacy work has helped shape renewable energy legislation in North Carolina. The firm emphasizes community acceptance, aiming to deliver projects that are welcomed by their host communities.

Carolina Woodworks LLC operates from Lyman, South Carolina, in the Upstate region. The family-owned business draws on more than 30 years of hands-on woodworking experience passed through generations. The shop is led by craftsman Sean, who oversees design, construction, and installation of every project.

The company designs, builds, finishes, and installs fully custom cabinetry and architectural millwork. Its in-house shop produces kitchen cabinets, bathroom vanities, built-ins, entertainment centers, home office suites, and pantry systems. Work includes frameless, inset, face-frame, and partial-overlay construction, with dovetailed drawer boxes, BLUM soft-close hardware, and professional lacquer finishes applied on site.

Carolina Woodworks serves homeowners, custom home builders, remodelers, interior designers, and commercial clients throughout the Upstate. Projects range from single-room built-ins to whole-home cabinetry packages for new construction and renovation.

The firm emphasizes four pillars: exact-design flexibility tailored to each home's architecture, technical range covering multiple cabinet configurations under one roof, furniture-grade execution with precision joinery and specialized finishes, and personal accountability through direct communication and disciplined installation.

name: Carolina Yarn & Fabrics Inc
old_description: Carolina Yarn and Fabrics, LLC, based in Laurens, SC, is a leading manufacturer and principal supplier of highly engineered fabric-formed concrete erosion control and scour protection systems. These systems have been utilized for more than 40 years around the world.
about:
Carolina Yarn & Fabrics Inc operates from Laurens, South Carolina. The company traces its origins to 1984 when the ARMORFORM trade name was established for fabric-formed concrete revetments.

The company manufactures ARMORFORM fabric-formed concrete systems for erosion control, scour protection, and lining applications. Its process involves weaving double-layer geotextiles from polyester or nylon yarns, which serve as forms for casting high-strength, fine-aggregate concrete. The forms can be placed underwater or on dry land. The company also provides engineering support, project management, and field services.

Carolina Yarn & Fabrics serves engineering firms, government agencies, and commercial contractors across infrastructure, water management, environmental protection, industrial, and energy sectors. Notable projects include the Endicott Island installation inside the Arctic Circle, MSHA-approved mining applications, U.S. Navy underwater pipeline and cable protection, and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers' Olmsted Locks and Dam scour protection.

The company emphasizes engineered products backed by comprehensive technical support and responsive delivery, which it says drives repeat business from long-standing clients. It positions itself as a partner that assembles multidisciplinary teams to deliver sustainable solutions, focusing on meeting client expectations for delivery, innovation, quality, and service.

name: Carpenter Co
old_description: Carpenter Co. is the world’s largest vertically integrated manufacturer of polyurethane foams, and serves a diversified global marketplace with polyurethane chemical solutions, polyester fibers, and insulation materials through a network of more than 60 production locations.
about:
Carpenter Co. is headquartered in Moore, Oklahoma, and traces its origins to 1950 when it began as a local latex foam manufacturer. The company has since grown into the world's largest vertically integrated producer of polyurethane foam and specialty polymer products, though ownership details and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

Today, Carpenter operates more than 60 production locations worldwide and employs over 6,500 people. Its core manufacturing includes polyurethane foams, polyether polyols (a key component in flexible urethane foams), polyester fibers, and insulation materials. The company maintains state-of-the-art research and development facilities in Richmond and other sites, where expert teams design innovative products and conduct rigorous in-house testing. Recent innovations include the patent-pending Casper Core+ technology aimed at improving mattress recyclability.

Carpenter serves a diversified global marketplace, with noted customers in the medical field (where it provides tailored protection products), mattress manufacturing, transportation (including a dedicated Carpenter Transportation team), and travel and leisure sectors. The company's domestic mattress manufacturing operations have been highlighted for supporting American jobs and local communities.

The company emphasizes its purpose, vision, mission, and values as guiding principles, alongside a code of conduct and ethics. Environmental stewardship is a stated focus, with efforts to enhance quality of life while preserving the planet. Vertical integration and a global footprint are cited as key differentiators, enabling control over the supply chain from chemical solutions to finished foam products.

name: Catamount Solar
old_description: At Catamount Solar, we deliver the advantages of solar energy to all of our commercial and residential  customers. Our employee-owners have a strong commitment to delivering the best possible renewable energy solutions to our customers every day. We bring decades of skill, experience, and enthusiasm to both residential and commercial solar. We provide good-paying jobs and profit sharing to our member owners. And we donate 5% of our profits to local community organizations.
about:
Catamount Solar, based in Randolph, Vermont, was established in 2011 as a worker-owned cooperative. The company began with a mission to help families, farms, and businesses reduce dependence on fossil-fuel energy through solar power. Ownership is structured as a member-owned cooperative where all workers are either members or on a track to become member-owners.

The cooperative designs and installs solar power systems for residential, commercial, off-grid, and battery backup applications. Its technicians bring decades of combined experience to each project, handling system design, installation, and ongoing service. The company does not disclose facility size or headcount, but emphasizes that employee ownership leads to low turnover and a stable, experienced installation crew.

Catamount Solar serves residential homeowners, agricultural operations, commercial businesses, and institutional clients such as schools. Notable projects include installations for Crossett Brook Middle School in Duxbury, and residential systems for customers in Woodstock and Thetford. The company works with clients of all sizes seeking energy independence and cost savings.

The cooperative model is central to its differentiation: employee-owners share profits through patronage dividends and participate in governance. Catamount Solar donates 5% of annual profits to Vermont community organizations. The ownership structure is intended to ensure long-term warranty support and continuity, as the company is less likely to be sold.

name: Central Carolina Plastics Inc
about:
Central Carolina Products, Inc. operates from Burlington, North Carolina, where it was founded in 1993 as a minority-owned, family-operated business. The privately held company has grown to occupy two facilities — a new plant built in 2003 and a second acquired in 2008 — serving customers worldwide from its Piedmont Triad location.

The company specializes in custom injection molding of thermoplastics using 61 microprocessor-controlled presses ranging from 40 to 1,650 tons. Its capabilities extend to scientific molding (RJG/Kistler), insert and over molding, hot oil molding, and sequential valve gate control, complemented by robotic extraction, custom end-of-arm tooling, and automated material handling. Value-added services include assembly, decorative coating, design and development support, tool construction and repair, and laboratory validation testing.

Primary customers are automotive OEMs and tier suppliers — General Motors, Lear Corporation, IAC, and Tower Components appear in testimonials — along with industrial manufacturers such as Stanley Black & Decker and Xylem. The firm is registered to ISO 9001:2015 and NSF/ANSI 61, and follows AIAG quality standards.

Central Carolina Products positions itself as a single-source provider, combining molding, finishing, and assembly under one roof in a climate-controlled environment. The company emphasizes engineering collaboration, process capability (CPK) monitoring, and APQP/PPAP compliance as differentiators rooted in its founding goal to deliver dimensionally critical and cosmetically perfect parts.

name: Central Kentucky Sonar
old_description: Like most anglers, I started fishing as a kid.  Bluegill fishing with my dad and younger brother.  The passion has stayed with me my whole life.  Being a weekend warrior in my first boat, didn't give me enough time on the water to learn my electronics.  I didn't know where to go or who to ask for help, even though electronics were much simpler then.  So I started Central Kentucky Sonar to help people learn as much as possible with hands on teaching.
about:
Central Kentucky Sonar operates from Nicholasville, Kentucky, where it was founded by an avid angler who grew up bluegill fishing with his father and brother. Frustrated by the lack of hands-on guidance for marine electronics, he launched the business to teach fellow anglers how to use their sonar and GPS units effectively. The company remains independently owned and operated.

The shop functions as a full-service marine electronics retailer: it sells fish-finding and navigation units, handles professional installation on customers’ boats, and provides one-on-one training sessions tailored to each angler’s needs. The owner emphasizes a personal, undivided-attention approach rather than group classes, helping clients interpret sonar returns, adjust settings, and integrate electronics into their fishing strategy.

The customer base consists of recreational and tournament anglers, boat owners, and anyone upgrading or switching brands of marine electronics. Central Kentucky Sonar serves the broader recreational fishing industry across central Kentucky, with clients ranging from weekend hobbyists to competitive bass fishermen seeking to maximize their on-water efficiency.

The venture began because the founder could not find a local resource for learning electronics when he bought his first boat. That gap drives the company’s differentiator: personalized, on-the-water-style instruction that turns complex electronics into practical fishing tools. The business also acts as an ambassador for the Jessamine County Homeless Coalition and sponsors the Jessamine County Food Pantry, reflecting a community-first ethos.

name: Central Metal Fabricators, Inc.
old_description: Since 1980, Central Metal Fabricators, Inc. has provided innovative design, fabrication, and assembly services to a diverse range of industries. We stock over 800 different parts, and have the documentation to manufacture thousands more.
about:
Central Metal Fabricators, Inc. (CMF) was founded in 1980 in Farmingdale, New Jersey, beginning as a welding and repair shop. Over more than four decades, the company has evolved into a full-service designer and fabricator of precision components and assemblies.

Operating from a 35,000-square-foot facility, CMF employs approximately 25 skilled personnel dedicated to design, fabrication, and assembly. The shop offers laser cutting, CNC milling, turning, punching, and bending, along with MIG and TIG welding, mechanical and electrical assembly, wire and cable manufacturing, and industrial sewing for strap assemblies. The company stocks over 800 parts and maintains documentation for thousands more, supporting both prototype and production runs.

Approximately 95 percent of CMF’s work serves the United States Armed Forces, with the remainder going to commercial, industrial, medical, pharmaceutical, research, and food-preparation sectors. The company supports major military installations including Aberdeen Proving Ground, Picatinny Arsenal, Tobyhanna Army Depot, and Naval Air Systems Command, providing replacement parts for legacy systems such as the Trojan V3 Communication Shelter and Prophet Control.

CMF emphasizes a track record of zero financial defaults, zero litigation, zero lost-time injuries, and zero adverse actions from the EPA, OSHA, or NJDEP. The firm also differentiates itself through reverse-engineering expertise for obsolete or defective parts and a commitment to traditional business values.

name: Central Montana Food Hub
old_description: Central Montana Food Hub is your source for high quality local food. Ordering from Central Montana Food Hub helps to build and support our local producers, and to preserve our precious agricultural land for sustainable future use.
about:
Central Montana Food Hub operates from Martinsdale, Montana, as an aggregator and online marketplace connecting local farms with consumers and wholesale buyers across central Montana. The hub was established to simplify the process for farmers to meet growing demand for local, sustainable food, though its founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The hub manages an online platform where customers order locally sourced meat, produce, eggs, honey, grains, and other products for weekly home delivery or free pickup at designated community locations. It coordinates logistics for delivery routes covering Martinsdale, White Sulphur Springs, Harlowton, Lewistown, Big Timber, Livingston, and surrounding areas, with ordering open Thursday through Sunday and deliveries on Tuesday and Wednesday. For wholesale customers—including restaurants, institutions, and retailers—the hub offers bulk options and customized recurring orders on the same weekly schedule.

The hub serves direct consumers as well as food-service and retail establishments such as Wild Oats Bakery, Jesse Peppers Smoke Shack, The Mint Bar, Musselshell Steakhouse, Gally’s Brewing Co., and grocery stores including Lewistown Town and Country, Midtown Market 2, and Castle Mountain Grocery. It also maintains a presence at the Harlo Farmers Market in Harlowton and the White Sulphur Springs Farmers Market.

The organization states its mission is to build and support local producers and preserve agricultural land for sustainable future use, providing farmers with marketing, selling, packaging, and delivery services so that fresh, healthy food reaches buyers throughout the region.
